'''Maria Fidecaro''' (1930-2023<ref>{{cite web | url=https://home.cern/news/obituary/physics/maria-fidecaro-1930-2023 | title=Maria Fidecaro (1930 – 2023) }}</ref>), née Cervasi,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maria Fidecaro Cervasi |url=https://www.hommages.ch/fr/avis-de-deces/maria-fidecaro-cervasi |access-date=2024-04-04 |website=Hommages |language=fr}}</ref> was an Italian [[Experimental physics|experimental physicist]] with a focus on [[particle physics]]. She has spent most of her career at [[CERN]], where she after retirement had the status of honorary member of the personnel.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title = Maria and Giuseppe: Lives intertwined with CERN's history {{!}} CERN|url = http://home.cern/cern-people/updates/2014/02/maria-and-giuseppe-lives-intertwined-cerns-history|website = home.cern|accessdate = 2015-11-30}}</ref>

Maria received her degrees in Physics from the [[Sapienza University of Rome|University of Rome]] in the 1940s.<ref name=":0" />

In 1954, she obtained a fellowship from the [[International Federation of University Women]] to do research at the [[University of Liverpool]] where she also defended her master thesis.<ref>{{Cite thesis |title=Positive pion - proton scattering in the range 10-35 MeV |url=http://cds.cern.ch/record/2307509 |publisher=Liverpool U. |date=1956 |first=Mario |last=Fidecaro}}</ref> In July 1955, she married [[Giuseppe Fidecaro]], a fellow physicist.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title = 50 years ago...|url = https://cds.cern.ch/journal/CERNBulletin/2010/07/News%2520Articles/1237563?ln=en|website = CERN Document Server|accessdate = 2015-11-30}}</ref> In 1956, Maria obtained a CERN fellowship. She was among the pioneering scientists at CERN since the establishment of the institution.<ref name=":0" />

== Scientific research ==
After Maria's marriage, she and Giuseppe carried out experiments on [[pions]]. Maria worked with a [[diffusion chamber]] and Giuseppe with a lead glass [[Cerenkov counter|Cherenkov counter]].<ref name=":0" />

Maria and Giuseppe were also involved in [[cosmic rays]] experiment in the [[Italian Alps]] just after the war. The experiment was set at 3,500 meters on the face of [[Matterhorn]], using a detector of 1-square meter.<ref name="Mermin Director"/>

After Maria and Giuseppe moved to [[Geneva]], Giuseppe was assigned to the [[Synchrocyclotron]] Division. The Synchrocyclotron was the first accelerator to be built at CERN in 1957. Meanwhile, Maria worked on a novel method to provide polarized proton beams to be used for particle collision in the accelerator.<ref name=":0" />

Throughout her career as an experimental physicist, she co-signed close to 200 publications.<ref>{{Cite web|url = http://inspirehep.net/author/profile/M.Fidecaro.1|title = Inspire author profile: Maria Fidecaro|date = |accessdate = 9 July 2016 |website = Inspire}}</ref>

The majority of her research relates directly to the experiments, including interpreting the measurements and results in the search for new particles. In Maria's early works in the 1960s, she studied the [[nucleon]]-nucleon charge exchange [[scattering]],<ref>{{cite report |last=Fidecaro |first=Maria |display-authors=et al. |date= April 1961 |title=Nucleon-nucleon charge exchange scattering at 26 GeV/c |url=https://cds.cern.ch/record/299895 |publisher=CERN |docket= CERN-NP-Internal-Report-61-1}}</ref> recorded data on high-energy [[Classical electromagnetism|electrodynamic]] processes.<ref>{{Cite book|title = Data on high-energy electrodynamic processes|url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/1160504?ln=ja|via = CERN Document Server|accessdate = 2015-11-30|year = 1962}}</ref>

Her research work also tackled the phenomenon of [[proton]]-proton [[elastic scattering]].<ref>{{Cite web|title = Analyzing Power A_nin High P-Transverse Squared Proton-Proton Elestic Scattering - INSPIRE-HEP|url = http://inspirehep.net/record/878030?ln=en|website = inspirehep.net|accessdate = 2015-11-30}}</ref> In the 1990s, she investigated the design and test of a prototype gas-sampling electromagnetic [[calorimeter]] of high [[granularity]]<ref>{{Cite journal|title = Design and test of a prototype gas-sampling electromagnetic calorimeter of high granularity for the CPLEAR experiment|url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/236714|journal = Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment|pages = 453–457|volume = 321|issue = 3|doi = 10.1016/0168-9002(92)90055-9|first1 = R.|last1 = Adler|first2 = G.|last2 = Backenstoss|first3 = P.|last3 = Bloch|first4 = D.|last4 = Damianoglou|first5 = P.|last5 = Dechelette|first6 = M.|last6 = Dröge|first7 = C.|last7 = Felder|first8 = W.|last8 = Fetscher|first9 = M.|last9 = Fidecaro|bibcode = 1992NIMPA.321..453A |year = 1992}}</ref> and collaborated on the construction of a position-sensitive [[photon]] detector for the [[CPLEAR experiment]].<ref>{{Cite journal|title = The CPLEAR electromagnetic calorimeter|journal = Nuclear Instruments and Methods in Physics Research Section A: Accelerators, Spectrometers, Detectors and Associated Equipment|date = 1997-05-11|pages = 293–320|volume = 390|issue = 3|doi = 10.1016/S0168-9002(97)00397-5|first1 = R.|last1 = Adler|first2 = G.|last2 = Backenstoss|first3 = F.|last3 = Bal|first4 = O.|last4 = Behnke|first5 = P.|last5 = Bloch|first6 = D.|last6 = Damianoglou|first7 = P.|last7 = Dechelette|first8 = M.|last8 = Dröge|first9 = B.|last9 = Eckart|bibcode = 1997NIMPA.390..293A |url = https://cds.cern.ch/record/318496/files/ppe-96-191.pdf}}</ref> CPLEAR experiment aims to carry out precision measurements of [[Charge parity|CP]], [[T-symmetry|T]] and [[CPT symmetry|CPT]] violation of the neutral [[kaon]] systems.

Maria's other work focused on [[phenomenology (particle physics)|phenomenological]] aspects of particle physics. She studied the fundamental [[Symmetry in quantum mechanics|symmetries]] in the neutral [[kaon]] systems. By the measurements of interactions and [[Particle decay|decays]] of neutral kaons, new and detailed information was found on [[CPT invariance]] in time evolution and decay. The newly achieved level of precision of the experiments called into question the validity of some of the often tacitly assumed hypotheses in particle physics.<ref name="FidecaroGerber2006">{{cite journal|last1=Fidecaro|first1=Maria|last2=Gerber|first2=Hans-Jürg|title=The fundamental symmetries in the neutral kaon system—a pedagogical choice|journal=Reports on Progress in Physics|volume=69|issue=6|year=2006|pages=1713–1770|issn=0034-4885|doi=10.1088/0034-4885/69/6/R03|bibcode=2006RPPh...69.1713F|arxiv=hep-ph/0603075}}</ref><ref name="FidecaroGerber2006Erratum">{{cite journal|last1=Fidecaro|first1=Maria|last2=Gerber|first2=Hans-Jürg|title=Erratum: The fundamental symmetries in the neutral kaon system—a pedagogical choice|journal=Reports on Progress in Physics|volume=69|issue=10|year=2006|pages=2841|issn=0034-4885|doi=10.1088/0034-4885/69/10/C01|arxiv=hep-ph/0603075|bibcode=2006RPPh...69.2841F}}</ref> She was also involved in an experiment looking for [[neutron-antineutron oscillations]] at the [[nuclear reactor]] of the [[Institut Laue–Langevin|Institute Laue-Langevin]] at [[Grenoble]].<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1985-06-13 |title=Experimental search for neutron-antineutron transitions with free neutrons |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/037026938591367X |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en-US |volume=156 |issue=1-2 |pages=122–128 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(85)91367-X |issn=0370-2693|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Maria was also involved in the search for [[CP violation|CP-violation]] (charge-parity violation) in the [[NA48]] experiment. After the theory of CP-violation in the decay of neutral kaon system was experimentally confirmed, the discovery brought the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] in 1980 to the discoverers of the theories, [[James Cronin]], and [[Val Fitch]]. The discovery played an important role in helping scientists explain the dominance of [[matter]] over [[antimatter]].

== Personal life ==
Maria and Giuseppe Fidecaro were the first few scientists among a total of 300 to 400 staff when CERN was first founded. During their time, few people could do experiments at CERN. Maria started with a group of only three scientists.<ref name="Mermin Director">{{Cite web|url = https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NX0cu52d-QE|title = CERN People- We are the memory|date = September 16, 2014|accessdate = |website = |publisher = UK: Crow Hills Film|last = Mermin (Director)|first = Liz}}</ref>

The couple, having devoted 60 years to research at CERN since its beginning, was seen as a living memory of the institute.<ref name=":0" />
